name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Full lifecycle: greenfield genesis (/spec:genesis, including an in-driver taste-funnel explore state and design-ratification state) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → optional /spec:design (mock-bound, deterministic fidelity gates) → /spec:build (direct Sonnet worker dispatch per layer wave, executed red-check) → /spec:review (spec-review-driver.js stepped, driver-stepped: deterministic legs via review-legs.js + ONE fresh-context reviewer whose non-soft findings carry executed repros; verdict derived by verdict.js) → /spec:release, plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.47.0 — viewport adaptation as a rendered rule (specs/20260831/02-viewport-adaptation-rules.md): design-atlas.js's static viewport-meta/dark-block matrix checks never measured whether a mock actually adapts at its declared viewports, so a phone-only mock ratified clean and the render gate later misattributed its non-adaptation to components (prax, spec 20260823/11). render-rules.js's closed renderCheck.kind set gains `no-overflow` (page scrollWidth vs clientWidth OR any non-exempt entry's right edge past clientWidth, fixed/outOfFlow/dataPositioned/srOnly exempted, fail-closed on a missing page block) and `line-length` (warn-only, estimated-width-and-character-count double condition, skips silently below its minViewport gate); render-inventory.browser.js adds a guarded top-level `page: { scrollWidth, clientWidth }` capture, schemaVersion unchanged. Zero wiring changes: /spec:sketch exit's existing render-gate --mocks call is the enforcement point once a host's manifest carries the new rules (design-rules.json ships both, `no-mock-overflow` at error/grounded and `line-length` at warn/taste). design.md now names rendered adaptation via render-gate --mocks as the real matrix verification and the static atlas checks as preconditions only. 7.46.0 — replay range materialization (specs/20260831/01-replay-range-materialization.md): a `diff.dirty:true` review row's judged range is completed by the close commit that follows it (range-identity spec 20260824/06 D3/D7), but replay's baseline worktree stood only at the close commit's parent — fix-worker edits that rode the close commit made legs green over the judged tree go red at the bare parent, and step 7 rung 3 recorded a false `leg-caught` (the live upwell incident). `--setup` gains `--overlay <closeSha>`: after standing the worktree up at `--commit`, it re-applies the close commit's non-meta delta (everything outside `specs/`, `.claude/`, `docs/canonical/`) as one build-shaped commit, materializing the range's true upper bound while keeping the three review-outcome surfaces blind at the parent; `--overlay` must be a strict descendant of `--commit` or the setup is refused. replay.md's own invocation always passes `--overlay {commit}`; `--setup` without it stays byte-identical to before. Step 7 rung 3 gains a pristine-baseline verification before `leg-caught` is ever recorded: a still-red leg after the retry now gets `git reset --hard HEAD^` (drops exactly the mutation commit) plus a fresh legs run — green there confirms `leg-caught`, still-red routes to rung 4's question seam instead of misrecording. 7.45.0 — review sidecar gitignore provisioning (direct fix 2026-08-31, cross-repo report from hearwell): spec-review-driver.js keeps its re-entry sidecar at specs/<date>/<spec>.review/ for the run's whole lifetime (deleted only at DONE), but init-gen.js provisioned no ignore entry for it — only .claude/worktrees/ — so a host gateCommand sweeping the whole tree (hearwell: prettier --check . inside pnpm gate, twice in one session) redded on the review run's own scratch and hard-stopped at GATE_RED before reviewer dispatch, and a close-time blind git add could sweep the sidecar into the host's history. IGNORE_ENTRIES gains specs/**/*.review/ with a child-path probe sample per the D4 idempotency lesson (specs/20260822/02); ensureGitignore's existing check-ignore probe makes the append idempotent and existing hosts pick the line up on their next init generate/--refresh. Behavioral pin executes git check-ignore against a sidecar child path after generate (red-verified against the pre-fix script). No standing guard: the fix lands inside the existing deterministic provisioner, below core § Incident Policy's admission bar.
